This is the recipe for a curative potion that will temporarily relieve the victim of the effects of a specific poison. 

Lord Antoine Baccha, Vizier de Guise needs this recipe before he can leave Undermountain.

Swirling darkness that draws the eye and almost blanks out the mind fills this small orb. Spending more than a few seconds staring into the darkness fills you with a dread and you can certainly understand why a beholder like G'zhorb would be bothered by such a seemingly insignificant thing.

G'zhorb will be anxious to get this back.

This is the opened document that you were retrieving for Harat. This is a list of the occupants of the Abyss, including Harat, who is rated as a minor demon of little power and not the God which he claims to be. No wonder he was so anxious to keep this from getting out.

Hilgoth was the king of the storm giants, a long time ago. Murdered at his own wedding, his corpse was lost for ages. All that is left of him now is his finger bone, polished to a sheen and still bearing the wedding band that magically clings to the finger. The finger bone makes an excellent staff.

The Widow Hagatha has asked that you find and return this staff to her.

This is a packet of papers, sealed with an unrecognizable seal. According to Harat, God of Darkness, this is a contract between him and Halaster. 

You could break the seal, but it might upset Harat.

The Sacarab Amulet of Imaskar is an amulet that Halaster uses to crush the will of Maggris, the Hive Mother. Without it, the creature and her minions would have left Undermountain.

Maggris awaits your return and the return of this item that she may die peacefully in her ancestral home.

The Wake and Shake foodstuffs company are an inter-dimensional group of illithids who provide these delicacies to any creature who can pay. Though an exotic treat, these have become a favorite amongst the many legions of evil creatures in Undermountain. The concept is simple, just take the bottle, shake it until the fairy wakes up, then throw the bottle in boiling water or cover it with warm ashes in a fire pit until done. Once you pop the cork, dinner is served.

The heads of state are a collection of decapitated heads, stolen from graves and tombs of nobles and politicians from the surface. What started off as a prank by a group of goblins has turned into a game in Undermountain, where different tribes of monsters will try to collect these heads. The more heads a tribe has, the more prestige they get. The original tribe of goblins has made huge amounts of gold, supplying a steady stream of heads for the Undermountain collectors.

Many times a group of monsters will inhabit Undermountain long enough for Halaster to get to know some of the individuals. While he is relatively hard-hearted towards their fates, he does occasionally find a young monster, which he finds cute. He will then, sometimes, leave little treats for the little creatures. These treats are welcomed by different monsters in different ways. The lollys are tasty to some, but some creatures have had trouble with them. One baby beholder got the sticky lolly stuck to his main eye and went blind. A young drow ate one, but got so sticky that he was eaten by a giant spider. Heedless of endangering the young creatures, Halaster still delights in leaving such treats around.

As disgusting as they sound, dire rat droppings are a basic ingredient for many damaging potions. Mixing the droppings with certain types of venom can cause an explosion, varying in size from the blow-your-hand-off to the cave-in a mountain variety. Even more destructive is the mixture of the droppings with black dragon saliva, which is credited to have destroyed an entire army when they accidentally dropped a vial of the mixture while carrying it to a catapult. Obviously, of the two substances, the dire rat droppings are far easier to find.

In an attempt to brighten up Undermountain, Halaster tried to cultivate a plant that could live in almost complete darkness, breeding ferns with moss. While it did work to a degree, the plants were rather ugly and tended to choke each other out, if kept anywhere near each other. There are still a few around, but Halaster seems to have given up on his experiments in this direction. The few plants that survive are often tended by ogres, or raised for trading with ogres, who find the plants make comfortable hats. The roots will often grow down into the ogre's skull, a sensation they have come to enjoy. Ogres are known for neither their intellect, nor their fashion sense.

These were once all the rage in Waterdeep, but became obnoxious so quickly that many found their way into sewers and trash heaps, and then later into Undermountain. The hummingbear was a gift item that had a minor enchantment making the small, blue, bear statue seem to dance and sing whenever anyone went near it. Though many were rightfully smashed in righteous anger, no small number were simply thrown out and later collected by small, inevitably evil and stupid creatures that took them back down into Undermountain and used them as wards around their lairs.

A Red Wizard once thought to set up an Enclave in Undermountain, catering to the monstrous, but often wealthy, population. Halaster didn't like that idea much and turned the Red Wizard into a jackal, stating that it wasn't really much of a change. He then took all the valuable merchandise, leaving behind a large amount of treasure to be spread amongst the denizens of his realm. The Thayan torture device is a simple object that one places on the skull of an enemy, muttering the command word, and then the device begins to rotate, back and forth. Very slowly it drills into the skull of the one being tortured. It takes a while, but is terribly effective, if you have the time to kill.

How so many flasks of whiskey managed to be disbursed through out Undermountain, no one is willing to say, especially not Mirt, whose profit margins have only increased throughout the last years. However it happened, the orcs and trolls of Undermountain have recently fought several small wars over the exquisite substance, each blaming the other for hording quantities of the drink. Unbeknownst to either group, it is actually the yuanti who have been gathering up the flasks and using them in a holy ritual to bathe in before battle. Coincidentally, the incidents of trolls attacking and devouring the snake-like people have increased lately, so it seems likely that someone might catch on, eventually.

A little over fifty years ago, a game arose amongst the denizens of Undermountain, called the Dread Lord's Dance. It was supposed to be named in honor of a lich who ruled a small portion of the third level, but it soon became a mockery. The game was played with two teams of ten, who would dance around an area in an intricate pattern, while maneuvering a ball on a string, swinging it past the heads of the other players, without touching. One day a team of ogres was competing against a team of goblins and one of the ogres clobbered a goblin, knocking his head in. This seemed like so much fun that the rules were quickly changed to make the point of the game to knock the opponent's head in with the ball. The game quickly became terribly popular with all, except the goblins. Even the Dread Lord was quoted as saying, "I rather fancy this version more than the first. I just wish my team, the Seven Step Skeletons, was more accurate."

The ball used for the game is difficult to produce, making it a popular prize for such competitions.

Across Faerun, everyone knows Volo and his travel guides. And while many of the denizens of Undermountain are illiterate, those who are not usually enjoy a hearty guffaw at what they call Iolo's Jokes. Volo himself might not approve, as much of what this audience considers jokes are some of his more serious works and some of his best poetry. But who is to say whether an audience is right or wrong. Should Volo ever deign to traverse Undermountain, he would likely be considered something of a folk hero there.

As hard as it is to believe, Undermountain is home to some of the best sales-creatures in Faerun. One particularly impressive merchant was a succubi, who always sold unusual items to unsuspecting monsters. Helesti is reported to have sold lava rocks to fire elementals, chunks of ice to yeti, and monocles to beholders. 

One of her most profitable endeavors was her discovery of the lucky former djinni lamps. First of all, she explained, there was once a powerful being trapped inside the lamp, and then the creature won its freedom, so how much more evidence could you need? When some would wonder how to tell that a djinni once inhabited the lamp, she would show them the magical residue left behind. Certainly, some creatures questioned how the magical residue looked an awful lot like ashes, but there were more than enough believers to win her the Sales-demon of the Year award.

Another of her imaginative devices was the snow globe of prophesy. According to her story, and a sworn affidavit from some goddess with messy handwriting, the snow globe would reveal secrets to its possessor, if one could stare at the globe for long periods, between shakes. She would then demonstrate by having a member of her audience (for she always drew quite a spectacle) sit, shake and stare. Then she would ask pointed questions, always leading to something they wanted out of life and then swearing that they could see it happening in the globe. This was a wildly successful technique, until word got around that several people she has promised great power were slaughtered the same day by adventurers.

The Succulent Soother was designed for baby monsters, which were always giving away their parent's lairs and hiding spots with squawking and squalling. Sales were excellent at first, except that the monsters quickly began to realize that their toothsome offspring were chewing the things to bits at a rapid pace. When one baby harpy got a piece of the soother stuck in its throat, a general uproar went around, with parental concern for the welfare of the children. Luckily for Helesti, the aggravated mob ran into a wandering band of shades, who had no sympathy and slaughtered the entire group.

Popular amongst young, female monsters, Waymoot Wendy set a trend for collectable dolls through out the northwest. At one time the dolls would say a variety of slogans when the little tots would pull a string, but the magic has long since worn off. Still, phrases like, "I love being devoured by you," or "You are the scariest monster ever," can often be heard repeated throughout Undermountain and in goblin tribes everywhere.

Some of the most puzzling and sought after artifacts in Undermountain are Criptin's Unidentifiable Objects. No one knows what they are, what they do or why Criptin made them and hid them all over the dungeon, but everyone wants one. Rumor has it that these objects contain unspeakable power, if only one could figure out how to make one work. No one has figured them out, or at least not done so and lived to tell the tale. Cautious collecting has become the key word for these items, yet ever once in a while, someone will try to collect a large number of them for completely mysterious purposes.

Erwin Entwhistle is a deep gnome resident of Undermountain who likes to invent things, much like many of his surface cousins. Not well-liked by his own kind, Erwin has managed to make friends with many of the other peoples of Undermountain. One of Erwin's friends is a duergar ant farmer, whose crops of ants were always getting eaten by hungry pests. Jazel, the duergar, had heard of Erwin's inventions and came to him for something to keep the ant poachers away. Erwin came up with an unusual trap that exudes a scent similar to that of an ant. When the hungry pests come sniffing about, looking for prey, they stick their noses in the trap, thinking there must be some ants inside, and the open end of the trap snaps shut, closing off the olfactory senses and rendering the pest helpless. Smaller predators are also trapped, but usually are either crushed or trapped inside completely. Other creatures have since sought these traps out, just to keep the pests away from their lairs.

A blacksmith, named Shaky, in Undermountain once created a self-replicating link of chains, thinking that he would break the spell once he had a long enough chain. Unfortunately, the replication process only created two loops that were linked, over and over again. Seeing he had failed, Shaky tried to stop the spell, only to find that he had no idea how to do so. The room filled with chain links so quickly that Shaky was crushed to death before he ever thought to leave the room. His death stopped the spell, but there were enough chain links that when an orc patrol opened the door, they took all the links and began to use them as a form of currency. Many of these links are still in circulation today.

Erwin Entwhistle is a deep gnome resident of Undermountain who likes to invent things, much like many of his surface cousins. Not well-liked by his own kind, Erwin has managed to make friends with many of the other peoples of Undermountain. One of his friendships is with a young, red dragon. The friendship was built when Tristonimix, the dragon, was pining about being stuck in Undermountain, in a part that was nothing like the smoky caves of his birthing place. Erwin overheard this and decided to do something about it. He created a huge amount of disks that would slowly burn bat droppings for long periods of time. With enough of these placed in the cave, Tristonimix felt just like he was at home again, including the odor of burning dung. Every once in a while Erwin will make a new batch of the disks, to replace all the ones stolen by kobolds.

How exactly do you feed an entire dungeon full of monsters during adventurer downtime? If your monsters aren't well-fed, they will typically turn on one another and you run out of monsters. That's why Halaster developed his patented Boneless Plantmeat. Shaped like an adventurer, this plant grows in almost any kind of light and provides all the vitamins and minerals a monster needs to grow strong and healthy. Although Halaster was trying to grow a version that had bones, the plants kept uprooting themselves and escaping. It is rumored that one of these plant-men escaped Undermountain and today runs one of the most successful greenhouses in Waterdeep. Much to the disappointment of those monsters who like to crack a good bone now and then, Halaster discontinued the bone-bearing Plantmeat.

Erwin was once considered prey, and while being hunted, he dropped a mechanical jumper he had just built. The harpy saw the jumper and reacted by dropping to grab what it thought might be a nice snack. Not only did it miss the first time, but seven times after that, getting madder and madder. The harpy matron happened upon the scene and saw how poor her underling's aim was. She was quite upset and ended up convincing Erwin to make a large number of the hoppers to use as training. While the harpies were recently slaughtered in a war between the surface and the drow, the hoppers have leaped their way into the many recesses of Undermountain.
